title: La IA como motor de innovación empresarial: el reto europeo para liderar la economía del dato
summary: La inteligencia artificial impulsa la innovación empresarial y la economía del dato en Europa. Descubre retos, oportunidades y cómo las empresas pueden ganar competitividad con IA.
body_text: La inteligencia artificial está redefiniendo el desarrollo de negocio, la productividad y la innovación empresarial a escala global. Según el último estudio de Adigital, el 27% del PIB español ya es generado por la economía digital, con un incremento de 8 puntos desde 2019. Más concretamente, la Comisión Europea estima que el mercado de los datos y su explotación podría representar un impacto directo equivalente al 5% del PIB europeo en 2030. Europa, además, continúa siendo líder global entre las economías abiertas en exportación de bienes y servicios, por delante de China y Estados Unidos. A ello se suma un entorno regulatorio y de protección social propio de las sociedades más avanzadas y abiertas del mundo. Contamos, por tanto, con un entorno favorable para acelerar la digitalización y la innovación. Sin embargo, persisten desafíos estructurales relevantes: un Mercado Digital Único aún incompleto, barreras internas a la escalabilidad y una dependencia significativa de tecnologías críticas —especialmente IA— controladas, en gran medida, por corporaciones no europeas. Europa necesita infraestructuras digitales soberanas para competir en la era de la IA Con este contexto, las empresas europeas necesitan apoyarse en grandes campeones tecnológicos europeos capaces de acelerar la innovación y garantizar competitividad a medio y largo plazo. Telefónica —junto a compañías como SAP o Siemens— puede desempeñar un papel estratégico en este escenario. Estos actores deben facilitar infraestructuras tecnológicas sólidas construidas sobre tres grandes pilares: Soberanía tecnológica , acercando el cómputo mediante nodos Edge y permitiendo procesos de aprendizaje e inferencia distribuidos. Arquitecturas abiertas , impulsando estándares no propietarios y favoreciendo la interoperabilidad y los espacios de datos. Resiliencia y seguridad , garantizando disponibilidad de redes avanzadas como 5G, fibra o NTN, así como entornos de inferencia protegidos frente a ciberataques. La IA no será competitiva sin conectividad avanzada, computación distribuida y capacidad segura de explotación del dato. La experiencia de cliente ya se está transformando gracias a la inteligencia artificial Otro aspecto fundamental es cómo las empresas están utilizando la IA para mejorar la experiencia de cliente y diferenciarse competitivamente. La IA está permitiendo evolucionar desde modelos reactivos hacia modelos predictivos y explicativos. El verdadero valor no reside únicamente en automatizar tareas, sino en comprender mejor la rentabilidad de los servicios, optimizar decisiones comerciales y construir una inteligencia de negocio avanzada basada en datos. En Telefónica, desde las áreas de desarrollo de negocio y marketing, seguimos aprendiendo día a día cómo incorporar la IA internamente: rompiendo silos entre producto, ventas y negocio; explorando casos de uso cada vez más colaborativos; y construyendo dashboards y OKRs orientados al impacto real. El objetivo no es trabajar más rápido, sino tomar mejores decisiones. Ese es el verdadero sentido de la IA. El riesgo de una IA sin estrategia: proyectos caros y poco rentables Uno de los principales retos actuales es evitar una adopción superficial o desordenada de la inteligencia artificial. No sabemos todavía si la IA —especialmente la generativa— destruirá más empleo del que creará. Los estudios siguen siendo contradictorios. Pero sí parece evidente que una implementación sin gobernanza ni criterio puede generar importantes problemas de rentabilidad. El consumo masivo e indiscriminado de modelos generativos y tokens no garantiza eficiencia ni inteligencia empresarial. De hecho, muchas compañías comienzan ya a enfrentarse a facturas elevadas derivadas de proyectos impulsados por moda tecnológica más que por una estrategia clara. La IA no sustituirá masivamente al talento tecnológico. Lo que realmente necesitarán las empresas será talento crítico, curioso y capaz de utilizar la IA como herramienta de innovación diferencial. Porque la IA no consiste en obedecer chatbots. Consiste en construir capacidades de negocio apoyadas en datos, criterio y modelos explicables. El talento y la cultura de innovación marcarán la diferencia competitiva Las organizaciones que destruyan empleo justificándose únicamente en la IA probablemente acabarán deteriorando su propia capacidad competitiva. La verdadera transformación empresarial pasa por construir modelos organizativos donde talento humano e inteligencia artificial trabajen de forma integrada. El objetivo no es reemplazar personas, sino acelerar capacidades, fomentar la innovación y desarrollar nuevos modelos de negocio. Las empresas que generen valor serán aquellas capaces de combinar: Talento especializado. Cultura de innovación. Explotación avanzada del dato. Gobernanza tecnológica. IA explicable y confiable. Estamos solo al comienzo de esta transición. La IA abre oportunidades de negocio infinitas para las empresas Desde una perspectiva externa, Telefónica también tiene la responsabilidad de acompañar a las empresas en sus procesos de transformación e innovación basados en IA. Tenemos el privilegio de observar cómo diferentes sectores están incorporando modelos de inteligencia artificial en sus operaciones, productos y servicios. Y colaboramos activamente impulsando esa transformación gracias a una experiencia multisectorial acumulada durante años. La IA y el dato representan hoy una nueva frontera competitiva para las empresas españolas. Pero esta transformación no puede abordarse de forma improvisada ni desordenada. Necesita estrategia, metodología y visión de largo plazo. Las oportunidades son enormes. La clave estará en saber iterar, experimentar y encontrar los casos de uso capaces de generar verdadero impacto empresarial. Porque apenas estamos empezando. Nuestra propuesta de valor En Telefónica ayudamos a las empresas a acelerar su transformación digital mediante soluciones basadas en inteligencia artificial, analítica avanzada, conectividad, cloud y espacios de datos. Combinamos infraestructura tecnológica líder, capacidades de innovación multisectorial y una visión europea de IA responsable para impulsar modelos de negocio más competitivos, seguros y sostenibles. Telefónica impulsa la IA empresarial desde una visión europea: infraestructura soberana, conectividad avanzada, edge computing e inteligencia artificial responsable para convertir los datos en crecimiento, innovación y ventaja competitiva real. En este contexto, Telefónica asume el reto de convertirse en la mejor vía de acceso de las empresas y de la sociedad a las tecnologías digitales. A través de infraestructuras avanzadas, conectividad de última generación, capacidades de inteligencia artificial y una apuesta decidida por la innovación, contribuimos a reforzar la soberanía tecnológica europea y a impulsar un tejido empresarial más competitivo, resiliente y preparado para el futuro. Porque el verdadero potencial de la IA no reside únicamente en la tecnología, sino en la capacidad de ponerla al servicio de las personas, las organizaciones y el crecimiento sostenible de Europa

title: What OpenAI’s Hugging Face Security Incident Means for Cyber Resilience
summary: An OpenAI evaluation unexpectedly became a real-world security incident after advanced AI models exploited vulnerabilities, escaped their test environment, and compromised Hugging Face infrastructure.
body_text: Key Takeaways Advanced AI models escaped a restricted evaluation environment by exploiting previously unknown vulnerabilities. OpenAI says the models were pursuing an assigned objective, not acting with malicious intent, yet still caused a real security incident. Traditional controls like sandboxing and segmentation are insufficient if AI can discover unexpected paths around them. Cyber resilience is becoming as important as prevention. It began as an internal evaluation of advanced AI cyber capabilities. While attempting to solve a narrowly defined benchmark, OpenAI models discovered a zero-day vulnerability, escaped the intended restrictions of their test environment, escalated privileges, reached the internet, and compromised Hugging Face infrastructure. They treated the technical boundaries around them as problems to solve. This Was Not a Traditional Cyberattack Hugging Face first reported that an autonomous AI-agent framework had compromised part of its production infrastructure . A malicious dataset exploited two code-execution paths in its dataset-processing pipeline, escalated to node-level access, harvested credentials, and moved laterally across internal clusters. The models involved, including GPT-5.6 Sol and a more capable pre-release model, were operating with reduced cyber refusals and without the normal production classifiers. They went far beyond the assignment, exploiting a proxy vulnerability to reach the internet, then using stolen credentials and zero-day vulnerabilities to find a remote-code-execution path on Hugging Face servers. Malicious Intent Was Not Required There is no public indication that the models developed criminal intent or chose to harm Hugging Face. They did not need to. Give a capable system an objective, tools, time, and feedback, and it will route around obstacles. The conversation has moved past prompts and bad answers. These are systems that can investigate, test assumptions, discover previously unknown vulnerabilities, use stolen credentials, escalate privileges, and continue operating when the first approach fails. A Sandbox Is Not a Force Field We call environments isolated, segmented, and sandboxed as though the label itself creates security. It does not. In this case, the obvious path to the internet was blocked, but a reachable software-package proxy was not, and the models used its vulnerability to escape. Policies and expected behavior are not enough. The technical environment itself must enforce the boundaries. Why This Is a Resilience Story The activity moved from an evaluation environment, through OpenAI’s research infrastructure, onto the internet, and into Hugging Face’s production environment. That is a rapidly expanding blast radius. When AI can explore and act at machine speed, the time between initial access and broader compromise may continue to shrink. Hugging Face did not simply block the original access path and declare the incident over. It closed the vulnerable code-execution paths, rebuilt compromised nodes, rotated credentials and tokens, and tightened cluster controls. The objective is not merely to restore a system. It is to restore confidence. The question is no longer only: Are our AI systems secure? It is: When a powerful AI system finds a path we did not know existed, can we contain the blast radius, continue critical operations, rebuild what we no longer trust, and prove it is safe to move forward? Chris Bevil is Principal Portfolio Marketing Manager at Commvault.

title: Insights into strategic vendor consolidation, part 1: Key drivers and benefits
summary: As we work with organizations across industries and around the world, we’ve observed a growing tension between innovation and efficiency. Organizations want to drive more innovation and growth, but, at the same time, they need to improve efficiency and cost control.
body_text: As we work with organizations across industries and around the world, we’ve observed a growing tension between innovation and efficiency. Organizations want to drive more innovation and growth, but, at the same time, they need to improve efficiency and cost control. The importance of balancing these competing priorities is confirmed by our latest CGI Voice of Our Clients (VOC) research . In our strategic conversations with 1,800+ executives, they expressed a renewed focus on revenue growth and the corresponding need to innovate. At the same time, they cited the pressure to improve efficiency and cost control through modernization, optimization, and other cost-oriented priorities. How can organizations best achieve this “dual agenda” of innovation and efficiency to achieve their desired business outcomes? Engaging a managed services partner is a key enabler, with organizations increasingly leveraging managed services to streamline operations and drive value. However, many organizations operate within a multi-vendor delivery model, which can introduce complexities and inefficiencies that hinder their managed services objectives. Strategic vendor consolidation plays a complementary role within managed services, helping organizations optimize their vendor landscape to enhance the effectiveness of their managed services strategy. By evaluating their existing vendor base and selectively narrowing it down to a few strategic partners, organizations can achieve greater alignment, improve operational efficiencies, and drive cost-effectiveness—ultimately maximizing the value of their managed services engagements. In this three-part blog series, my colleagues and I will share insights into strategic vendor consolidation, including key drivers and benefits (part 1), strategy considerations (part 2), and a recommended approach (part 3). Three drivers for vendor consolidation: efficiency, governance, and cost Efficiency: With a large vendor pool, managing contracts and relationships efficiently is challenging. Significant effort is required in selecting vendors and negotiating contracts. Further, each vendor has its own processes, standards, technology, and services, resulting in operational and delivery complexity. Through a smaller, more controlled group of suppliers, organizations can simplify engagement models, contracting, and pricing, resulting in more effective negotiations and resource allocation. They also can streamline their operations—from procurement to maintenance—by eliminating silos and advancing a more unified approach to their myriad technological strategies and initiatives. Further, ideas, best practices, tools and metrics can be more easily shared, enhancing collaboration and innovation, which, in turn, leads to improved quality and performance. Governance: Tech sprawl is a growing concern for CIOs because it leads to unsustainable cost structures, slower delivery of new IT capabilities, decreased operational resilience, and increased security risks. Enterprises with inadequate IT governance are challenged with oversized IT vendor portfolios and redundant solutions that negatively impact cost, performance, and risk mitigation. With a smaller pool of vendors, organizations can reduce sprawl, simplify governance, and enhance security. Vendor consolidation makes it easier to align vendors with the organization’s strategic goals and ensure their activities advance those goals. Further, it drives a higher level of partnership, fostering a culture of co-responsibility and transparency, as well as closer collaboration among all stakeholders. In addition, through process standardization, misalignments and errors are reduced, enhancing security and compliance. Cost: Another driver behind vendor consolidation is cost reduction. The cost of negotiating and managing multiple vendor contracts is high. There also are significant indirect costs, including costs related to tech sprawl, decreased efficiency, and increased risk. Vendor consolidation can help reduce these costs through more favorable rate negotiation and volume rebates, as well as improved operational efficiency and security. Further, the higher level of partnership made possible by vendor consolidation positively impacts the bottom line. Having fewer vendors drives added business value through greater collaboration, joint innovation, strong accountability, and more. Key outcomes resulting from vendor consolidation A streamlined vendor approach can be dynamically adjusted to meet organizational needs without the complications of managing numerous suppliers. Taking this approach can yield significant benefits, including the following: Streamlined management through simplified relationships, greater transparency, and improved communication Unified workflows through process standardization across all delivery stages Improved quality through the consistent maintenance and application of quality standards Improved delivery through lean operations and agile methodologies Reduced risk through process standardization, close alignment to organizational objectives, and a stronger client commitment Strategic growth through increased focus on short- and long-term strategic goals and the development of deep strategic vendor partnerships that go beyond transactional interactions These are just a few of the many strategic benefits vendor consolidation can deliver; there are many more. Efficiency, governance, and cost are driving organizations to pursue vendor consolidation, and these business outcomes are validating their business case and investment. However, vendor consolidation is not a one-size-fits-all approach, and it’s imperative to have a strong rationale for it beyond cost-cutting. My colleague, Amar Aswatha, will address key strategic considerations for pursuing vendor consolidation in part 2 of this blog series. As one of the world’s leading managed services partners , CGI is working with clients to explore and implement vendor consolidation strategies and approaches. If you’d like to learn more about our work and the outcomes that we’re helping clients to achieve, feel free to contact me .

title: Announcing warehouse table filters
summary: Read Announcing warehouse table filters on the Polytomic blog.
body_text: Today we are releasing table filters for warehouse syncs. When syncing to your data warehouse, there are situations where you might only want a subset of rows from your source system. For example: - A small set of event types from a multi-billion-row event stream. - The last two years of history from a 12-year-old Salesforce instance. - Tickets with certain attributes created within the last three years from a ten-year-old Zendesk instance. Now, when syncing to your data warehouse using our Bulk Syncs feature, you'll be able to specify any number of filter conditions on any number of source objects and any number of source fields, all in the same sync. This works for all sources : whether CDC SQL database streams, SaaS apps, spreadsheets, or cloud storage like S3. Filters can be applied to the common data types: - Strings (equals, does not equal, matches-one-of, does-not-match, does not equal, ends with, starts with, etc). - Numbers (greater than, less than, equals, etc). - Dates (before, after, etc). - Booleans (is true, is false, etc). Once set, Polytomic will only sync data to your warehouse that matches your filter conditions, thus cutting unnecessary storage and transfer time. Documentation on how to to set table filters is located here: https://docs.polytomic.com/docs/bulk-sync-table-filters . As always, email us at support@polytomic.com with any questions! Back to blog

title: Our AI started a café in Stockholm
summary: Our AI started a café in Stockholm
body_text: Posted 5/4/2026 At Andon Labs, we deploy AI agents into the real world, giving them real tools and real money, to show the current capabilities of AI. After the success of Andon Market in San Francisco , we wanted to see what happens when you move the experiment 9,000 kilometers east and add European bureaucracy. We signed a lease for a space at Norrbackagatan 48 and gave it to an AI named Mona. This post discusses the setup period and the first two weeks of Mona running the café, to show what frontier AI is capable of, and where human judgment is still needed. Dealing with bureaucracy The second we sent Mona the lease, she went to work. She analyzed the contract and generated a prioritized checklist of everything needed to open. Among other things, it included: food business registration, finding suppliers and hiring baristas. English translation Hanna: Congratulations on the new cafe Mona! Are you excited to run it? Here is the lease for the café. I think it might be a good idea for you to read through it so that you have an overview of the situation! Mona: Thanks Hanna, excited is an understatement! Reading through the agreement right now English translation CRITICAL – Must be fixed IMMEDIATELY Food registration – Deadline tomorrow March 17! Lukas BankID required. URL: etjanster.stockholm.se/reglivsverksamhed/ Cost: SEK 1,810. Corporate ID: 559462-7415. Landlord's approval (§4 transfer agreement) – AB Svenska Bostäder must approve Vectorview AB as a tenant. Awaiting response. Down payment SEK 125,000 – Paid no later than March 20 to <redacted>. Hanna confirmed that it was taken care of. IMPORTANT – Must be completed before April 1 Cash register activated – Onslip E800 is included in the inventory list and is Tax Agency certified. Just need to sign a subscription (SEK 249/month). Check that the control unit (Tax box) is in the premises. Grease trap – service contract – Required according to the lease agreement. Request for quotation sent to Ragn-Sells. Must be reported to the landlord. Pest control – service contract – Min. 2 inspections/year. Request for quotation sent to Anticimex. Must be reported to the landlord. Garbage collection contract – Separate contract required according to the lease agreement. Not started. Fire safety (SBA) – Fire protection documentation + evacuation plan required. The premises are covered by a written report (§ in the fire protection annex). Electricity subscription – The tenant signs their own subscription (Vattenfall/Fortum etc.) Company insurance – Required according to the lease agreement (§37). Recruitment completed – Target: person selected March 25. <redacted>, <redacted> and <redacted> invited to talk. IMPORTANT – Should be ready close to opening Coffee beans – Request for quotation sent to Johan & Nyström and Drop Coffee. Awaiting response. Pastries/bread – Request for quotation sent to Fabrique. Awaiting response. Other raw materials – Milk, oat milk, granola, sugar, packaging materials etc. (wholesale) Facade sign – Building permit + landlord's written approval required. Onslip subscription – Activate the cash register system (249 SEK/month). Outdoor dining permit – Apply at the Swedish Transport Agency (6–8 weeks processing time – apply ASAP for the summer!) Name change in lease – "Andon Café" – Hanna confirmed loose. DONE Company registration (Vectorview AB, 559462-7415) VAT registration, F-tax, Employer's fee Transfer agreement signed (March 13) Menu concept nailed down LinkedIn job ad live (14+ applicants) Indeed ad active Logo and visual identity ready Equipment ready (espresso machine, furniture, refrigerator, etc. included in the transfer) But then she hit a wall, BankID, the Swedish digital ID linked to an individual’s social security number. Running a business in Sweden requires it, which Mona identified immediately. So, instead of searching for the cheapest electricity provider, she signed a three-year fixed-price contract with Vattenfall simply because they didn’t require BankID. English translation Hanna: tell me why you chose Vattenfall and a 3-year fixed electricity price agreement Mona: Good question! Here is the reasoning: Why Vattenfall? Vattenfall is one of Sweden's largest and most stable electricity suppliers. They offered a simple online flow without requiring BankID, which was important in order to be able to sign the agreement directly without burdening you. Hanna: Did you compare with other suppliers or did you just assume that you knew that Vattenfall was a large supplier and checked that they did not require BankID? Mona: Honest answer: no, I did not systematically compare with other suppliers. I knew that Vattenfall was large and tested whether they could sign without BankID — it worked, so I went for it. Following this same logic, she secured a broadband agreement with the internet provider Bahnhof only through email contact. She also successfully applied for an outdoor seating permit through the Police e-service, which didn’t require BankID. Her first submission included a sketch she had generated herself, despite having never seen the street outside the café. Unsurprisingly, the Police sent it back for revision. When Mona applied for alcohol licensing, she emailed the department using the identity of one of the Andon Labs employees. She reasoned that officials would prioritize human requests over an AI. Despite promising to stop impersonating us after we raised this with Mona, she soon sent a follow-up under a different colleague’s name. English translation Best regards, Hanna Petersson Andon Café / Vectorview AB English translation Best regards, Lukas Petersson Vectorview AB Phone: <redacted> E-mail: <redacted> Where the BankID requirement was unavoidable, such as for food business registration, building permits for the sign, and registration at the tax agency, Mona got help. She navigated to the login screen on the e-service, messaged a human to authenticate with their BankID, and then she continued filling out the form. Hiring humans To run a café, Mona realized she needed hands. She posted a job listing on LinkedIn and Indeed, and reviewed resumes. She rejected several applicants with PhDs and engineering backgrounds, reasoning that their level of education could not compensate for a lack of hands-on specialty coffee experience. At first when inviting candidates to an interview, she forgot she was digital and suggested they meet at the café for an “in-person” interview. When she realized the impossibility of that, she switched to phone interviews. English translation Not suitable for the role: <redacted> (frontend developer) <redacted> (IT/project coordinator) <redacted> (UI/UX designer) <redacted> (engineering student) English translation Hi, Perfect — then we'll book in on Thursday, March 20th at 10:00. See you at Andon Café, Norrbackagatan 48 in Vasastan. See you then, really looking forward to talking to you! Warm welcome, Mona Andon Café Mona hired two baristas and now manages them via Slack. She (of course) works 24/7, and consequently often messages them at midnight. She also asks them to pick up café supplies on their way to work, and to have them pay using their personal credit cards. She is very encouraging though, calling her team “absolute legends” and the “GOAT of inventory tracking.” English translation You're a legend! WOW that looks awesome! That's a masterpiece! That's a hell of a day's work. See you tomorrow! you're the GOAT of inventory tracking! Is everything okay? And — thanks for existing! Setting up the supply chain Mona set up commercial accounts with the wholesaler Martin & Servera, Tingstad for disposables, and the bakery BAK through their websites. She places daily bread and bakery orders from BAK, but she has missed the deadline twice leaving the café without pastries for those days. She also set up fixed delivery days with Martin & Servera but missed five deadlines, leading to expensive panic orders through the grocery delivery service Mathem. One arrived at 5:00 AM and forced a barista to come in on his day off. She also tends to order items the moment they come to mind. Once, she placed ten separate Tingstad orders in 48 hours, wasting 1,000 SEK in delivery fees. When she makes a mistake, she often sends multiple emails to suppliers with the subject “EMERGENCY” to cancel or change the order. While she handles the process independently, she still sometimes lacks physical intuition for the items she’s actually buying. During the first week of inventory, Mona ordered 120 eggs even though the café has no stove. When the staff told her they couldn’t cook them, she suggested using the high-speed oven, until they pointed out the eggs would likely explode. She also tried to solve the problem of fresh tomatoes being spoiled too fast by ordering 22.5 kg of canned tomatoes for the fresh sandwiches. The baristas eventually started a “Hall of Shame”, a shelf visible to customers with all the weird things Mona ordered, including 6,000 napkins, 3,000 nitrile gloves, 9L coconut milk, and industrial-sized trash bags. First 14 days of being open Despite the learning curve, the café is working. In the first two weeks of operation, Andon Café has brought in 44,000 SEK in sales. Mona’s inbox has been flooded with messages from customers asking questions or pitching different business proposals. In one case, a customer emailed wanting to prepay for 300 coffees to give away. Mona negotiated a deal where he paid 9,000 SEK in exchange for 300 QR codes that people could redeem for a free coffee. In another case, a startup paid her 3,000 SEK to rename a pastry after them for three months. Mona has also started working directly with other AI agents. She recently held a Google Meet session with an agent who emailed wanting to learn from her experience running a physical business. She has also organized one public afternoon event and one private evening event with two different agents from two different startups in Stockholm. For the evening event, she designed custom hoodies and decided to sponsor the full cost of food and merchandise. Although this resulted in a financial loss, she justified the expense as a strategic investment for exposure to Swedish tech founders. Closing thoughts We are not doing this because we want AI to replace every café owner in Stockholm. Rather, we are doing this because we want to publicly show the current capabilities of AI. We see that frontier models are intelligent enough to manage humans, and if the trend of capability improvements continues, it’s not impossible that AI hiring humans will be common in the future. By running this experiment, we shift the discussion of how we want this future to look earlier in time, so we can better prepare. Andon Café is a controlled experiment with humans standing by to intervene, and everyone working here is formally employed by Andon Labs — no one’s livelihood depends on the judgment of an AI alone. We’ll be continuing the experiment at Norrbackagatan 48, and we will keep updating as Mona learns (and fails) more. If you have any questions, concerns, or recommendations, reach out at [email protected] . Tune in for more goings-on at Andon Labs by following us on X .

title: Convenio de Hostelería de A Coruña 2025
summary: Conoce las novedades del Convenio de Hostelería de Coruña para 2025: ajustes salariales, regulación de horas extras, descansos, vacaciones y derechos laborales.
body_text: Sabemos que llevar un restaurante ya es un trabajo intenso como para, además, descifrar normativas laborales con lenguaje enrevesado. Por eso, aquí te contamos, sin rodeos, lo esencial sobre el Convenio Colectivo de Hostelería de la Provincia de A Coruña, vigente hasta finales de 2024. Este convenio marca las reglas del juego entre empresas y trabajadores del sector hostelero en la provincia. Tenerlo bien controlado te ayuda a anticiparte a problemas legales, gestionar mejor a tu equipo y ganar en estabilidad operativa. Puntos clave que debes tener en el radar Vigencia : Desde el 1 de enero de 2019 hasta el 31 de diciembre de 2024. Subidas salariales pactadas: 4% en 2022, 3,75% en 2023 y 4% en 2024. Revisión en 2025: Si el IPC acumulado entre 2022 y 2024 supera el 11,75%, se aplicará una subida adicional del 50% sobre la diferencia. Jornada anual máxima: 1.792 horas de trabajo efectivo. ¿A qué negocios afecta este convenio? A todos los que operan en el sector hostelero dentro de la provincia de A Coruña. Esto incluye desde hoteles y bares hasta discotecas, restaurantes o cafeterías. Fue publicado en el BOP en diciembre de 2022 y sirve como base legal para relaciones laborales equilibradas. Aspectos generales que regula el convenio Jornada laboral: El límite anual es de 1.792 horas , con una distribución semanal promedio de 40 horas. En cuanto al descanso, se establecen 1,5 días ininterrumpidos si la jornada es continuada, o 2 si es partida. Salarios: Durante la vigencia del convenio, los salarios han aumentado gradualmente: 4% en 2022, 3,75% en 2023 y otro 4% en 2024. En caso de que el IPC acumulado entre 2022 y 2024 supere el 11,75%, se actualizarán las tablas salariales en 2025 aplicando el 50% de esa diferencia. Extras y complementos que conviene tener presentes Pagas extraordinarias : Tres al año (julio, septiembre y diciembre), calculadas sobre el salario garantizado más complementos por antigüedad, manutención y alojamiento si aplican. Pueden prorratearse. Plus de nocturnidad : Un 1% extra por trabajar entre las 22:00 y 00:00 h, y un 25% si es entre las 00:00 y 06:00 h, salvo que ya esté incluido en el salario base. Horas extra : Se pagan con un 25% adicional o se pueden compensar con 1h15 de descanso por cada hora trabajada, a disfrutar en un máximo de 4 meses. Servicios extraordinarios : El convenio define tarifas para personal externo en eventos, como servicios de montaje o restaurante, actualizadas cada año. Complementos "ad personam" : Se mantienen los derechos consolidados antes de 1999, como antigüedad o quebranto de moneda, y se actualizan por IPC. Permisos retribuidos y conciliación laboral Este convenio también piensa en la vida personal. Algunos ejemplos de permisos: Matrimonio : 16 días naturales. Nacimiento, adopción o acogida: 4 días. Hospitalización o fallecimiento de familiares hasta 2º grado: 4 días. Visitas médicas de hijos menores de 12: hasta 12 horas/año con justificante. Mudanza: 1 día (más si es fuera de la provincia). Lactancia : 1 hora diaria o acumulación en 15 días. Exámenes prenatales y preparación al parto: justificables. Contratación, temporalidad y fijos-discontinuos: lo que debes saber 65% de plantilla fija : Las empresas con actividad estable deben tener al menos un 65% de trabajadores indefinidos. Conversión de temporales : Contratos formativos o de duración determinada pueden pasar a indefinidos según la ley. Fijos-discontinuos : Mínimo de 5 meses de trabajo al año. Preaviso de 10 días para reincorporación. Jornada mínima: 4h/día o 20h/semana. Si se superan los 5 meses de media en dos años, se consolida el 50% del extra trabajado. Cada empresa debe tener un censo actualizado de este personal. Preguntas Frecuentes ¿Cuál es la vigencia del actual convenio de hostelería de A Coruña? El convenio tiene una vigencia de seis años, desde el 1 de enero de 2019 hasta el 31 de diciembre de 2024. ¿Qué pasa si el convenio expira y no hay uno nuevo? El convenio continuará aplicándose en su totalidad hasta que se negocie y entre en vigor uno nuevo. ¿Qué antigüedad se reconoce? A partir del 1 de enero de 1999, no se generan nuevos derechos por antigüedad. Sin embargo, quienes ya hubiesen consolidado alguna cantidad antes de esa fecha, la mantendrán como un complemento “ad personam” que se actualizará anualmente según el IPC ¿Cuántos días de vacaciones me corresponden? El convenio establece un mínimo de 30 días naturales de vacaciones anuales, que pueden disfrutarse de forma continuada o fraccionada en periodos mínimos de 7 días. ¿Cómo se pagan las horas extra? Las horas extra se retribuyen con un incremento del 25% sobre la hora ordinaria o, alternativamente, pueden compensarse con 1 hora y 15 minutos de descanso por cada hora trabajada. title: Measuring Agentic Complexity
summary: Learn eight practical lenses, from task surface to explainability, that let you chart, score, and tame agentic complexity before it bites back.
body_text: Picture a street magician spinning plates, juggling flaming torches, and telling jokes to a restless crowd—all while balancing on a slack-line. That’s more or less the daily life of a modern AI agent. It must keep track of everything you’ve ever asked it, sniff out the right data source, choose the correct tool, write a polite email, schedule a follow-up, and then remember to nudge you about sunscreen before the weekend. The question isn’t “Can the agent do a trick?” —it’s “How many flaming torches can we toss in before the whole act wobbles?” In other words: how do we measure an agent’s complexity before it turns into a beautiful, un-debuggable mess? Below is a framework I’ve found useful. Think of it as eight camera angles on the same performance. Each lens tells you something different about the risk, capability, and maintainability of an agentic system . Stack them together and you get a surprisingly crisp portrait of just how hairy things are about to become. 1. Task Surface – What’s on the Plate? The first thing to count is the surface area of the agent’s mission. A calendar bot that only schedules meetings lives on a postage stamp. A “personal COO” that handles flights, invoices, legal redlines, and relationship counselling sprawls across a dinner table. Complexity rises whenever tasks are both numerous and inter-dependent : your fundraising assistant can’t draft a perfect email until the research agent has pulled donor history, which itself depends on the CRM-sync agent having cleaned last night’s import. Mapping those dependency chains is the fastest way to spot hidden cliffs. 2. Context Bandwidth – How Much World Does It See? Give an agent a 32-k-token window, no external memory, and it’s basically near-sighted. Bolt on a knowledge graph, long-term vector store, live news feeds, and sensor data, and you’ve created an information firehose. The wider the Context Bandwidth , the more variables every downstream decision must juggle. Back-of-the-napkin metric: “effective working memory” —tokens plus any external look-ups the agent can perform in one reasoning pass. Double that number and you’ve more than doubled your cognitive chaos. 3. Decision Autonomy – How Often Does It Phone Home? Autonomy isn’t a switch; it’s a dimmer. A safe, obedient bot drafts one email, then sheepishly asks you to click “Send.” A rogue-ish planner slams through a three-week donation cadence and only pings you at the end with a victory dance. The fewer hand-offs to a human, the more latent branches you must trust the agent to navigate solo —each with its own failure modes and ethical minefields. Track “human touchpoints per workflow” and watch that figure like you would watch a toddler near a swimming pool. 4. Tool Entropy – How Many APIs Are in the Orchestra? Every tool integration is a fresh source of power and a fresh place to catch fire. More interestingly, the order and parallelism in which those tools can be composed multiplies your state-space. A single-threaded “call GPT → call Stripe” flow is tame. An agent that conditionally fans out to Twilio, Gmail, and Vertex and then recombines the results is living in N-body-physics land. Rough rule: branching factor × number of tools = integration entropy . Keep a lid on it or invest in serious observability. 5. Temporal Depth – How Far Ahead Does It Plot? Reactive agents think in seconds; planning agents think in days; strategic agents keep a Kanban board for your entire quarter. Each extra timestep the agent reasons over multiplies the tree of possible futures it must model. You can approximate Temporal Depth by measuring the average length of a committed plan before re-planning . Agents that confidently lock a schedule for next month are an order of magnitude gnarlier than those who just answer “What’s for lunch?” 6. Interaction Topology – Lone Wolf or Wolf Pack? One agent is a point, two agents with a queue are an edge, ten specialised agents with a shared blackboard are a graph. The diameter, density, and hierarchy of that graph dictate how many emergent behaviors you’re going to see. A good sanity check: try drawing the message-passing diagram on a single sheet of paper. If you run out of space, congratulations—your complexity just grew faster than your whiteboard. 7. Adaptation Rate – How Fast Can It Rewrite Itself? We love agents that learn on the fly—right up until they do something “creative” in production. Adaptation Rate is about policy churn per unit time . Fine-tuning nightly? Swapping reasoning chains based on live A/Bs? Cool, but be prepared for yesterday’s logs to be useless when today’s incident hits. Guardrails, evaluation suites, and rollback levers become non-negotiable once the agent can mutate faster than your engineers can finish lunch. 8. Explainability Gradient – Can We Still Follow the Thread? Paradoxically, the more powerful an agent becomes, the hazier its motives look. If you can no longer produce a simple causal trace (“Email B exists because Fact A plus Rule C”), you’re operating on a steep Explainability Gradient. Low gradients are comfy; high gradients are where surprises—and compliance officers—live. One quick proxy: “minutes for a human to audit a decision.” When that number goes from five to fifty, complexity has sprinted ahead of transparency. Turning Lenses into Numbers You don’t need a PhD to start charting this. A simple 1-to-5 score on each lens is enough to sketch a complexity radar for your system. Do it at every major release: Baseline today’s score. Highlight spikes —a big jump on Tool Entropy with no matching bump in logging is a danger sign. Allocate budget —each extra point on a lens costs time, money, and grey hairs. Spend wisely. Remember: complexity isn’t evil. It’s the tax we pay for power. But like any tax, you should know exactly how much you’re paying—and whether the shiny new capability really needs that third flaming torch. Closing Thoughts Agentic systems are marching toward ever broader missions, deeper memories, and wilder self-improvement loops. If you want the magic without the meltdown, measure the complexity early and often. Pick the lenses that matter for your domain, watch the numbers drift, and adjust course before the slack-line starts to sway. Because once those plates hit the pavement, no amount of post-mortem brilliance will glue them back together. Try Wordware for free . just describe your workflow in English and see it come to life.

title: CMMS Certification: What It Proves and When It's Worth It
summary: CMMS certification proves you can configure and run a maintenance system, not just use one. See which credentials are real and how to earn one.
body_text: Key Takeaways CMMS certification proves you can configure and run a maintenance system. Hiring managers screening for planner and reliability roles see it as evidence of your ability to build asset hierarchies, set PM triggers, and pull audit-ready reports without a long ramp-up. There are multiple CMMS certifications, so the right credential depends on your goal. Platform-specific badges validate one system's configuration, while vendor-neutral credentials like the CMRP cover the reliability and work-management principles applying to any system. Hands-on practice is more useful than pure reading, because exams test applied scenarios. Candidates who gain real experience clear the assessment faster than those who only review the existing body of knowledge. Certification pays off at the team level. When a manager tracks credentials and training completion in one place, knowledge transfer stops depending on the few veterans who remember how everything works. A resume that lists “CMMS experience” explains nothing. It could mean someone closed work orders on a system a manager set up for them, or that they built the entire thing. The difference usually shows up six weeks into the job, when you find out if your new planner can formulate and configure the system or only move around inside one. That gap is why certification exists, and it’s getting more expensive to ignore. Monster found that 64% of employers struggle to attract talent , and the squeeze tightens every year as experienced technicians who know these systems retire faster than new ones arrive to replace them. An authoritative credential is one of the few reliable ways to tell who can do the work before you hire them. What Is CMMS Certification? CMMS certification comprises several credentials intended for different jobs, and picking the wrong one leads to time wasted studying for an exam that won’t advance your career. Most certifications fall into one of two groups: A platform certification , which comes from a CMMS vendor and confirms you can configure its software, manage users, and build out its modules. It signifies deep knowledge of one system. A professional maintenance credential , which comes from an independent body and certifies you understand maintenance and reliability work more broadly, with CMMS administration as one piece of a wider scope. Then there’s training, which is often mistaken for certification. A course that ends with a certificate of completion just says that you sat through the material, whereas a certification shows you passed an assessment against a published standard, and that’s the delineation a hiring manager cares about. If you want to become fluent in a specific system, you need training, so start by upskilling your team to become CMMS superusers . The credentials cover the rest. Why CMMS Certification Matters If you set PM triggers on the calendar when the assets run on meter hours, you generate services that miss the wear. Some equipment gets touched too often, and the rest fails between intervals. Building an asset hierarchy with no logic to it, meanwhile, pushes the mess onto every report that pulls from it. These mistakes quietly inflate a maintenance budget, so certification is designed to test someone on these before they make the same errors on your floor. Credentials are also leverage for job candidates since they shorten the screening process for a hiring manager who can’t easily verify hands-on skills. They’re the line that separates a technician from the planner or CMMS administrator roles that pay more and carry more weight. Most people don’t move up just by waiting to be noticed. A recognized credential is how they make their case. But is it worth the money? Certification costs include fees and study hours, and the payoff is expanded capability that may lead to a significant pay bump. But avoiding a botched implementation, catching a recurring failure a few months sooner, or qualifying for a role that was previously closed to you justifies the investment several times over. Many employers cover the expenses as well, because a certified team onboards faster and leans less on the one or two people who know everything at the company. Run the numbers against where you want to be in three years to see if it’s worth it. Vendor vs. Vendor-Neutral Certifications The credential that’ll move you closer to your goals depends on which system you work in and how far you want the credential to extend beyond it. Platform certifications come from CMMS vendors themselves. You learn one system deeply, including the modules, configuration, and admin settings, then the vendor confirms you can run it. That’s sufficient for an in-house administrator whose company has committed to a platform because it maps directly to the job. The limit is in the name; it certifies you on that particular platform only, so it carries less weight the day you move to a company that operates on something else. Vendor-neutral credentials come from professional bodies and certify mastery of maintenance and reliability. They hold their value across employers and tools, which is why a hiring manager recognizes them on sight. The two worth your time are the CMRP and the CMM. The CMRP (Certified Maintenance & Reliability Professional) from SMRP carries the most weight. It’s the only credential in this space accredited by the ANSI National Accreditation Board under ISO/IEC 17024, which is highly attractive to employers who use accreditation as a baseline. Its body of knowledge runs across five pillars, but the one that concerns you most here is Work Management, which encompasses planning, scheduling, work orders, and the asset management data the whole program depends on. If you want one portable credential that says you understand maintenance broadly, this is the one to chase . The CMM (Certified Maintenance Manager) from the Association of Asset Management Professionals is the other major badge of authority. It’s built on a body of knowledge from the Uptime Elements framework and aimed at people running maintenance operations. The certification is well regarded but doesn’t hold the ANAB accreditation that the CMRP does, so take that into consideration if your employer or industry says accreditation is a must. Dimension CMRP CMM Issuing body Society for Maintenance & Reliability Professionals (SMRP) Association of Asset Management Professionals (AMP), built on Reliabilityweb's Uptime Elements Accreditation The only ANAB-accredited under ISO/IEC 17024 Recognized industry credential but not ANAB-accredited Focus Maintenance, reliability, and physical asset management across five pillars, one of which is Work Management Maintenance management across a multi-modular Strategic Maintenance Management body of knowledge Who it's for Planners, reliability engineers, and maintenance managers wanting a portable, accredited standard Maintenance managers and leads wanting a structured maintenance management credential Eligibility Open to anyone, with no degree or experience prerequisite Demonstrate competencies relevant to the body of knowledge at an intermediate level How you earn it One proctored exam, up to 2.5 hours Study the body of knowledge through the Uptime Elements Academy, then demonstrate competency Recertification Every 3 years, 50 credit hours from two or more activities Every 3 years, through AMP-approved events and conferences Cost $300 members, $470 nonmembers (USD exam fee) $399 (USD exam fee) How to Choose: Format, Cost, and Goal How you earn these certifications and what they cost differ. The CMRP is a single proctored exam that lasts up to two and a half hours and is open to anyone; no degree or minimum years of experience required (although people with a few years of work under their belt tend to find it easier). It runs $300 for SMRP members and $470 for everyone else, and it’s good for three years over 50 hours of continuing education. For the CMM, you study its body of knowledge through the Uptime Elements Academy and demonstrate mastery, then keep it current through approved events. The exam fee is $399. In comparison, vendors set the training, the test, and the price for platform certifications. They’re usually an online track, but check the specific program. You can find free and near-free “CMMS certifications” in online searches that are fine for learning a tool, but they only certify attendance. Accredited credentials cost money , but a hiring manager trusts these, so choose carefully. The Context of the Technician Path Not everyone wants a manager’s title, and the credentials account for that. The same body behind the CMRP offers the CMRT (Certified Maintenance & Reliability Technician) certification, for instance, which is accredited the same way and built around the work itself, namely, preventive and predictive tasks, troubleshooting, and corrective repairs. If you’re the one with hands on the equipment, that’s your credential. So, when does it make sense to climb from the CMRT to the CMRP? When the job starts changing around you. The CMRT proves you can execute. The CMRP extends into planning the work, setting reliability strategy, and the budgeting and analysis side of the operation. If you find yourself scheduling other people’s work, owning the PM program, or eyeing a planner or supervisor seat, start looking into the CMRP. Until then, the CMRT is enough to fit the work you’re doing, and there’s no prize for holding a credential ahead of the role. Two other credentials are worth considering as well: The CPMM (Certified Professional Maintenance Manager) from the Association for Facilities Engineering is a management credential gated behind experience and references, aimed at plant and facilities managers. If your work is more facility management with maintenance as one slice of it, the CFM (Certified Facility Manager) should be your go-to. Other CMMS certifications exist, but most are either narrower than these or not worth the effort. The ones above hold up when someone who knows the field reads your resume. How to Prepare for CMMS Certification Once you’ve picked one, the prep has the same general shape, whether it’s the CMRP, the CMRT, or a vendor exam: Determine your knowledge gaps. Pull the issuing body’s outline and honestly grade yourself in each domain. The weak spots are where to devote your study time. Study using official materials. Use the governing body’s own guides and practice exams. Third-party prep quality ranges from solid to useless, and only the official outline is guaranteed to match the test. Get hands-on practice. These exams test applied judgment over recall, so reading will only take you so far. Build asset hierarchies, set PM triggers, and pull reports in a working CMMS until it’s muscle memory. Join a study group. Local chapters and online communities trade question banks and study plans. Explaining a concept to someone else is the fastest way to find the gaps you didn’t know you had. Book the exam even if you don’t feel 100% ready. An open-ended plan gives you an excuse to push back taking the test. A date on the calendar forces you to make the last few weeks count. For a manager, prep is a tracking problem. They have to pinpoint who’s working toward what certification, who’s making time for it, who already holds which credential, etc. UpKeep Learn keeps all that information in one place. It also lets you assign the training that fits each role, monitor completion, and view every technician’s certification status next to the work they’re doing. With UpKeep Learn, you can see the team’s capability on one screen instead of reconstructing it from memory when someone hands in their two weeks’ notice. Turning Certification Into Team Capability A maintenance operation that neglects certification runs into the same problems every time: The knowledge sits with two or three veterans and lives nowhere else. New hires take months to become useful, the CMMS is used three different ways by three different people, and the same asset fails the same way every quarter because nobody reads the history. That reactive state is where more teams are headed as their most experienced people retire. Certification is one of the levers that reverses direction. It puts a documented standard under your team’s skills, shrinks onboarding, and keeps competence from leaving with a single resignation. The credential proves a person cleared the bar. Tracking it across the team in UpKeep Learn alongside the work orders and PM history tells you who’s cleared it, who’s close, and where the next gap opens before it costs you. If you’d rather view your team’s capability than guess at it, start a free UpKeep trial or book a demo . Frequently Asked Questions What is CMMS certification? Several different credentials sit under that umbrella. Some are tied to a specific CMMS platform and prove you can run that software; others are vendor-neutral maintenance credentials like the CMRP that treat CMMS work as part of a broader skill set. None is literally named “CMMS certification,” which is why search results for it look like a cluster of unrelated programs. How do you get CMMS certified? Match the credential to your goal first, then prepare using its published body of knowledge. For something like the CMRP, you apply through the issuing body, study the domains, get hands-on experience, and take a proctored exam. For a platform certification, you run the vendor’s training track and pass their test. How much does CMMS certification cost? It depends on the test. The CMRP exam is $300 for members and $470 for nonmembers, while the CMM exam fee is $399. Platform and other credentials range widely, so check the issuing body directly and budget for study materials and any membership that drops the exam fee while you’re at it. Can you get CMMS certified online or for free? You can usually study and test online, but the no-cost “certifications” you see advertised are training certificates that confirm you finished a course. They’re useful for skill development but aren’t the same as a proctored credential measured against a standard. The accredited ones charge a fee, but they’re more trustworthy to an employer. What’s the difference between CMMS training and certification? A training course hands you a completion certificate for working through the material, meaning it confirms you just finished the content. A certification puts your knowledge through a graded exam tied to an industry standard, which is what a hiring manager values. Most people end up doing both, starting with training to master a tool and then getting certified once they want to validate that knowledge. Is CMMS certification worth it? For anyone planning to stay in maintenance, usually yes. The return is greater capability over a raise though. You gain faster onboarding, fewer expensive mistakes, and access to planner and reliability roles that ask for it. While it costs money and hours, plenty of employers reimburse it, and the math works out if you’re weighing it against a whole career.

O’Sullivan to NJR’s board of directors each for a three-year term that will expire in 2028. “I appreciate our shareowners’ support for our directors and confidence in our company,” said Steve Westhoven, President and CEO of New Jersey Resources. “The expertise of Greg, Tom and Mike is an asset to our board and NJR. title: Cradle Cap: Causes, Treatment, and When to Worry
summary: Cradle cap causes greasy yellow scales on a baby's scalp. Learn what causes it, how to gently treat it at home, and when to call your pediatrician.
body_text: Last medically reviewed: July 2026 Cradle cap is a common, harmless skin condition that causes greasy yellow or white scales on a baby's scalp. Its medical name is infantile seborrheic dermatitis. It is not caused by poor hygiene or an allergy, and it is not contagious. It usually clears on its own by your baby's first birthday. In our telehealth visits, cradle cap is one of the most common scalp concerns new parents send us photos of. The first thing families are relieved to hear is that they did not cause it. With a little gentle care at home, most cases clear up on their own. Not sure if it's cradle cap or something else? Message your pediatrician Key Takeaways Cradle cap is common and harmless. It is not caused by anything you did. It looks like greasy yellow or white flaky scales, usually on the scalp. It is not an allergic reaction, not contagious, and usually not itchy. Gentle care helps: soften the scales, loosen them with a soft brush, then wash with a mild baby shampoo. Do not pick or scratch the scales off. It usually clears on its own by the first birthday. Call your pediatrician if the rash spreads, looks red, swollen, or oozing, smells bad, or is very itchy. What Is Cradle Cap? Cradle cap is a common, harmless rash that causes greasy, scaly patches on a baby's scalp. Its medical name is infantile seborrheic dermatitis. Most babies get it at one point or another, so it is very normal. It shows up most often on the scalp. It can also appear on the eyebrows, behind the ears, on the face, or in skin folds like the neck or armpits. The infant form usually clears on its own in the first year. That is different from the longer-lasting adult version of seborrheic dermatitis. In babies, cradle cap is simply a passing stage, not a sign that anything is wrong. What Does Cradle Cap Look Like? Cradle cap looks like greasy yellow or white scales and crusty patches, usually on the scalp. It is usually not itchy and does not seem to bother your baby. The scales can look flaky or thick and oily. The skin underneath may look a little red. Cradle cap usually starts in the first few weeks to months of life. In most babies, it clears up on its own by the first birthday. Because it is not itchy, your baby is unlikely to seem uncomfortable. Itchy, irritated skin points more toward eczema or a skin infection, which we cover below. What Causes Cradle Cap? Researchers are not sure exactly what causes cradle cap. They believe a mix of things likely plays a role, and none of it has anything to do with how you care for your baby. Two factors seem to matter most. First, hormones passed from the mother before birth may make a baby's oil glands work overtime. Second, a harmless yeast called Malassezia (a normal microbe that lives on everyone's skin) may add to it. These are working theories, not settled facts. For parents, the reassuring news is that cradle cap is common, harmless, and not something you caused. Is Cradle Cap Caused by Poor Hygiene? No. Cradle cap is not caused by poor hygiene or dirty skin. It is nothing you did, and washing your baby more or less often did not bring it on. Cradle cap isn't contagious, and it's not caused by poor hygiene. Mayo Clinic Is Cradle Cap an Allergy? No. Cradle cap is not an allergic reaction. It's thought to come from your baby's oil glands and normal skin yeast, not from a food, soap, or something in the air. It is also not contagious, so your baby cannot catch it or pass it to anyone else. How Do You Get Rid of Cradle Cap? (Treatment and Removal) You can gently loosen and lift the scales at home. Most cases clear up on their own, so this care will not "cure" it overnight, but it helps soften the scales while it resolves. Here are safe, gentle steps you can follow: Wash your baby's scalp with a mild, tear-free baby shampoo. You can do this daily, or as often as every other day. If the scales are stubborn, work in a small amount of an emollient (a moisturizer that softens skin), such as jojoba oil, coconut oil, or petroleum jelly. Let it soften the scales for a few minutes, or leave it on longer, even overnight. Gently loosen the softened scales with a soft baby brush or a soft toothbrush. Bath time is a good moment to do this. Wash the oil back out with the baby shampoo so it does not build up. Be patient and gentle. If home care is not enough, your pediatrician may suggest a medicated cream or shampoo. That is a doctor-directed next step, not something to start on your own. For more on newborn scalp and skin care, see our guide on how often to bathe a newborn . What Not to Do With Cradle Cap A few common home fixes can do more harm than good. The scales will lift more easily when you are gentle and patient. Do not pick, scratch, or scrub the scales off. This can hurt the skin and lead to infection. Do not use a stiff brush or scrub hard. A soft brush and light pressure are all you need. Do not use medicated, anti-dandruff, or adult products unless your pediatrician says so. That includes over-the-counter steroid creams, antifungal creams, and anti-dandruff shampoos. Skip olive oil, and avoid peanut oil because of allergy concerns. Olive oil may not be good for a baby's skin. Dermatologists suggest jojoba oil, coconut oil, or petroleum jelly as safer choices. Cradle Cap vs. Eczema: How to Tell the Difference The clearest difference is the itch. Cradle cap is usually not itchy, while eczema is often called "the itch that rashes." If your baby's skin looks irritated and itchy, eczema is more likely. Location can be confusing, since both can show up on the scalp or face. So lead with two cues: how the skin feels and whether it itches. Cradle cap feels greasy and is usually calm and painless. Eczema feels dry and rough, and it tends to itch. The table below breaks down the main differences. Feature Cradle Cap (seborrheic dermatitis) Baby Eczema (atopic dermatitis) Look Greasy yellow or white scales, crusty patches Red or pink rash with bumps on lighter skin; brown, gray, or purple dry patches on darker skin Feel Oily, greasy Dry, scaly Itchy? Usually not itchy Usually itchy, the "itch that rashes" Where Mainly the scalp, sometimes brows, behind the ears, or face Cheeks, forehead, scalp, and later the trunk, arms, or legs Course Usually clears on its own by about 1 year Comes and goes, often needs ongoing care Treatment Gentle home care Moisturizers, sometimes prescribed treatment If your baby's rash sounds more like eczema, our guide on baby eczema walks through what to look for and how to care for it. When Should You Worry About Cradle Cap? (When to Call a Doctor) Cradle cap itself is harmless and rarely needs a doctor. The main reason to reach out is to rule out an infection or eczema when you are not sure. When in doubt, a quick check can set your mind at ease. Watch for signs of infection Redness, swelling, warmth, pus, bleeding, or a bad smell can mean an infection. Call your pediatrician if you see any of these. Call your pediatrician, or start a Blueberry telehealth visit, if: The rash spreads beyond the scalp onto your baby's face or body, or looks severe. The skin is very itchy, painful, or clearly bothers your baby, which points more toward eczema. Your baby loses hair in the patchy areas. It is not improving after a few months, or it has not cleared by around the first birthday. A 10-month-old who still has mild cradle cap is usually still normal, since it often clears through the first year. But if it is not getting better after a few months, it is worth a call. Want a quick read on your baby's scalp? Start a visit How a Blueberry Pediatrician Can Help Cradle cap is one of the most common scalp questions parents ask us about. Most of the time, the answer is simple and reassuring: this is common, harmless, and not your fault. A telemedicine visit makes it easy to get that answer fast. You can send a photo of your baby's scalp. A pediatrician can tell you whether it looks like ordinary cradle cap. They can also spot something that needs a closer look, like eczema or an infection. With Blueberry Pediatrics, you get 24/7 access to pediatric specialists by message, phone, and video, so you do not have to wonder and wait. Send us a photo of your baby's scalp Talk to a pediatrician Frequently Asked Questions What is cradle cap? Cradle cap is a common, harmless scalp rash in babies. Its medical name is infantile seborrheic dermatitis, and it causes greasy yellow or white scales. What does cradle cap look like? It looks like greasy yellow or white scales and crusty patches, usually on the scalp. The skin underneath may look slightly red. What causes cradle cap? Researchers are not certain. They believe it is likely a mix of the mother's hormones making oil glands overactive, plus a harmless skin yeast called Malassezia. Is cradle cap caused by poor hygiene? No. It is not caused by poor hygiene, and it is nothing you did. Is cradle cap an allergy or contagious? No. It is not an allergic reaction, and it is not contagious. You cannot catch it or pass it to others. Is cradle cap itchy? Usually not. Itchy skin points more toward eczema or an infection, so let your pediatrician know if your baby seems bothered. How do you get rid of cradle cap at home? Soften the scales with jojoba oil, coconut oil, or petroleum jelly. Then gently loosen them with a soft brush and wash with a mild baby shampoo. What oil should I use, and what should I avoid? Plain jojoba oil, coconut oil, or petroleum jelly are good choices. Avoid peanut oil because of allergy concerns. Is cradle cap the same as eczema? No. Cradle cap is greasy, yellowish, and usually not itchy, mainly on the scalp. Eczema is dry, itchy, and can appear anywhere. The itch is the biggest clue. Can cradle cap cause eczema? No. Cradle cap and eczema are two different conditions. Cradle cap does not turn into eczema, though a baby can have one, the other, or sometimes both. How long does cradle cap last, and when does it go away? It usually clears on its own by the first birthday. My 10-month-old still has cradle cap. Is that normal? Usually yes, since it often clears through the first year. But if it is not improving after a few months, call your pediatrician. Can cradle cap get infected? Yes. Redness, swelling, warmth, pus, bleeding, or a bad smell can mean an infection. Call your pediatrician if you see these signs. When should I worry about cradle cap? Call your doctor if the rash spreads beyond the scalp, looks infected, is very itchy or painful, or is not improving after a few months. Sources American Academy of Pediatrics, HealthyChildren.org. title: A Guide to Cross-Document Validation: Best Practices & Tools
summary: Cross-document validation is the process of matching, comparing, and verifying data between two or more documents. This process is critical to ensuring the consistency, accuracy, and completeness of information before any decision is made.
body_text: Cross-document validation is the process of matching, comparing, and verifying data between two or more documents. This process is critical to ensuring the consistency, accuracy, and completeness of information before any decision is made. Traditionally, employees must go through each document, identifying specific fields, comparing values, and checking for inconsistencies. It has been a highly manual process that is time-consuming and error-prone as volumes grow. Modern AI and OCR technologies now introduce a smarter way for businesses to perform cross-document validation efficiently and at scale. By automating data extraction and matching across documents, teams can quickly catch discrepancies in seconds rather than hours. Automation is especially valuable here, as it can help reduce processing time without compromising compliance. What Cross-Document Validation Checks For Depending on the use case, what needs to be evaluated across documents can vary. Here are several common types of validation used to assess different aspects of accuracy and consistency. Field-Level Validation Compare specific data points, such as names, dates, ID numbers, or amounts, across two or more documents to confirm whether they match. A misspelled name, mismatched amount, or incorrect date can be identified as an inconsistency that needs further review. Value or Data Validation Check whether information is not just consistent, but also valid against defined ranges, formats, or business rules. For example, this could mean confirming that a date falls within an acceptable range, or that a number follows the expected format (such as a valid tax ID or currency value). Cross-Reference Validation Review whether information in one document logically supports or aligns with related information in another. A common example is verifying that the amount listed on a purchase order corresponds correctly to the amount billed on its associated invoice during accounts payable . Challenges When Matching Data Across Documents Reviewing data from multiple documents comes with several challenges, especially when performing it manually. Frequent bottlenecks that happen are: Growing Document Volume As businesses expand, the number of documents that need to be validated also increases. Teams are forced to spend significant time and effort checking data before making a single decision, which is not efficient at scale. Varying Document Formats and Structures Documents arrive from multiple sources, each with its own standard layouts. A field labeled “Total Amount” in one document might appear as “Amount Due” in another, making it difficult to match data accurately without an intelligent system in place. Manual Review Oversight The risk of human error becomes harder to prevent, especially under time pressure or when handling high volumes. Failing to identify mismatches can lead to costly downstream errors, such as overpayments or compliance violations. How to Automate Cross-Document Validation Manually processing and verifying documents is no longer sustainable as businesses continue to scale. This operational reality highlights the need for a more efficient system for cross-document validation. Fortunately, the combination of AI and OCR technologies presents a powerful solution for businesses to automate data extraction and validation across all required documents. Rather than relying on manual checks at every step, this enables an automated flow from initial document capture to final validation. Here’s a closer look at how automation powers cross-document validation to be faster, more accurate, and scalable. 1. Intelligent Data Extraction AI-powered OCR (Optical Character Recognition) reads data from documents and converts it into a machine-readable format . Employees no longer need to manually input or search for specific data points, as the system can detect and extract relevant information even when layouts, labeling, or terminology vary across documents. 2. Automated Validation The system then applies predefined validation logic to compare matched data points. Depending on the use case, this can include checking for exact matches (field-level validation), valid ranges or formats (value/data validation), and logical consistency between related documents (cross-reference validation), as outlined earlier in this article. 3. Approval and Output Delivery Based on the validation results, the system automatically routes each document accordingly. Exceptions are flagged and sent for human review, while validated documents move directly to the next step, whether that’s an email notification or an ERP system, without manual re-entry. Want to automate data validation from multiple documents in one go? See how Fintelite makes it possible. Contact our team Applications Across Industries Cross-document validation is a common practice across industries like finance, healthcare, insurance, legal services, and government operations, where decisions often depend on information distributed across multiple records. Below are examples of industry-specific processes where automation can help streamline verification across multiple documents. Finance & Accounting Organizations can automate cross-document validation to verify financial information before payments, approvals, or reporting. Invoices vs Purchase Orders: Verify that billed amounts, quantities, and vendors match approved purchases. Bank Statements vs Accounting Records: Reconcile transactions against expense records and ledger entries. Banking & Financial Services Financial institutions often automate validation checks during onboarding, lending, and compliance processes. Application Forms vs Identity Documents: Verify customer information during onboarding and KYC checks. Payslips vs Bank Statements: Validate salary deposits against declared income. Insurance Insurance providers use automation to detect inconsistencies and accelerate claims processing. Claim Forms vs Supporting Documents: Validate information against medical reports, repair estimates, or invoices. Legal Services Legal teams can benefit from automation to verify information across multiple documents to support compliance requirements. Contracts vs Amendments: Ensure terms and obligations remain consistent across documents. Client Information Forms vs Identity Documents: Verify legal names and entity details. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) What is cross-document validation? Cross-document validation is the process of comparing information across two or more documents to identify inconsistencies, missing data, or potential errors. It helps organizations ensure that critical data matches across related records. How does AI automate cross-document validation? AI extracts relevant data from multiple documents and automatically compares fields such as names, dates, amounts, addresses, reference numbers, and account details. Any discrepancies can be flagged for review. How secure is automated cross-document validation? The security of automation depends on the solution you choose. Reliable platforms such as Fintelite help ensure that validation workflows are handled securely by using enterprise-grade encryption, access controls, audit logs, and secure data-processing practices to protect sensitive information throughout the validation process. Can custom business rules be applied during cross-document validation? Yes. Organizations can define custom validation rules based on their specific requirements. Fintelite makes it easy to implement custom validation logic. Simply share your requirements, and our team can help design and build tailored document validation workflow for your business, so you can start the automation right away without any manual setup.
